matches.title: mlw-1999-heritage
matches.note: Scott "The Fop" Rogers defended the MLW Heritage Championship on behalf of its absent champion, Lord James Gray, and intentionally lost, transferring the title to Devon Starr. The same broadcast unmasked the champion, revealed elsewhere on the card as "Lord James Gray," as the wrestler Derek "Sky" Walker.

matches.title: mlw-1999-heavyweight
matches.note: Triple threat rules. Eddie Van Gibson retained the MLW Heavyweight Championship after Reverend White narrowly failed to pin him.

matches.note: Triple threat rules. Scott "The Fop" Rogers won the MLW Heritage Championship from defending champion Devon Starr.
A chamber-of-death match for a guest championship, the IIWA Extreme Championship, not one of MLW's own titles; defending champion Doomsday survived Vic Valiant's challenge.

matches.title: mlw-1999-heavyweight
matches.note: Ladder match. Eddie Van Gibson retained the MLW Heavyweight Championship, pulling the flaming title belt down himself after the ladder caught fire.

A stipulation match for thirty days' control of the promotion: the High Society faction's David Klass won by count-out after the promotion's own president's own hired gun, Damien Lestat, struck the president with his own valet's cooler and walked out.

matches.title: mlw-1999-tag-team
matches.note: "Hard Time In The Hard Rock," a no-rules five-team brawl through a hotel bar for the vacant MLW World Tag Team Championship. Sons Of Savagery came out on top.

matches.title: mlw-1999-hardcore
matches.note: "Blue Jays Brawl," no disqualification inside a baseball stadium's own training and equipment rooms. Voodoo won the MLW Northern Hardcore Championship.

matches.title: mlw-1999-true-north
matches.note: A Royal Rumble for the vacant MLW True North Championship, drawing a larger field than is structured here. "No Worries" Rob Magnum won, eliminating Nevada Harris last.

matches.title: mlw-1999-heritage
matches.note: A reverse battle royal for the MLW Canadian Heritage Championship (wrestlers start backstage; the first man to reach the ring wins), drawing a larger field than is structured here. Champion Lord James Gray retained after The Cougar left Steve Lake unable to continue.
Main event #1, a buried-alive casket match ordered by the promotion's own president. Damien Lestat won by burying Zombie Rogers alive; when officials dug up the coffin afterward, it was empty.

matches.title: mlw-1999-heavyweight
matches.note: Main event #2, a double scaffold match for the vacant MLW World Heavyweight Championship: the first man to reach the belt hanging between two scaffolds would win. A returning masked wrestler powerbombed Devon Starr off the top scaffold, clearing the way for Valtharius the Mad to claim the belt; a further returning wrestler appeared, unbilled, at the close.

name: A World of Pain, Day One

date.source: The promotion's own broadcast, self-dated as Day One of a three-day pay-per-view.

matches.stipulation: Fifteen-man battle royal, five wrestlers from each of the three allied federations
matches.note: Two outside interferers eliminated one wrestler with a pair of powerbombs to the arena floor before the field was cut to two; the eventual winner tricked the runner-up into being counted out.

matches.stipulation: No-disqualification street fight
matches.note: Fought through a parking lot with car doors, frying pans and a table; the winning side's own pinning wrestler had been unconscious for several minutes before his partner rolled him onto the equally unconscious loser for the cover.

matches.stipulation: Steel cage match
matches.note: The promotion's own Vice President revealed he had quit to join his opponent's own faction, locking the promotion's own president inside the cage with them; a ring-floor explosion then introduced a masked new arrival who chokeslammed a manager through the canvas before the bell was rung to end the match without a decision.

matches.stipulation: Elimination-style triangle match; the winner advances to the newly created interfederation championship's first match
matches.note: The last elimination came from a legdrop off the top rope.

appearances.source: Presented the promotion's own newly created championship trophy in the ring before the opening match.
Appeared alongside the promotion's own president to present a newly created championship trophy.

evidence.source: The promotion's own broadcast, now served in full.
evidence.note: Opens a three-day interfederation pay-per-view uniting three allied Usenet promotions under a shared banner.

notes: Introduces a shootfighting trophy division for the host promotion, and stages the debut of a masked new enforcer during a Vice-Presidential defection angle.

name: A World of Pain, Day Two

date.source: The promotion's own broadcast, self-dated as Day Two of a three-day pay-per-view.

matches.stipulation: Texas Tornado match for the Tag Team Championship
matches.note: The winning team's own manager, a masked cult figure, praised the outgoing champions' cruelty and shook their hands after the match.

matches.stipulation: Inaugural Cruiserweight Championship match
matches.note: An unidentified interferer resembling a wrestler from another federation hit the loser with a Tiger Driver before the winner's own finisher sealed the pin.

matches.stipulation: Cage match for the Rio Grande Championship
matches.note: The champion retained by leaping from the top of the ten-foot cage for the pin.

matches.stipulation: Caged triangle match; the winner earns a future Canadian Heavyweight title shot
matches.note: A table set alight during the match badly burned one competitor's face; the winner finished the other with a Tombstone Piledriver.

matches.stipulation: Interfederation eliminator; the winner advances to Day Three's newly created championship match
matches.note: The loser was caught with a dropkick and finished with a double underhook facebuster.

evidence.source: The promotion's own broadcast, now served in full.
evidence.note: Two title changes, a title defense, and the second of two interfederation eliminators setting up Day Three's championship match.

notes: Continues the three-day interfederation pay-per-view begun the prior night.

name: A World of Pain, Day Three

date.source: The promotion's own broadcast, self-dated as Day Three of a three-day pay-per-view.

matches.stipulation: Title versus career match for a title shared with an unrelated federation
matches.note: The challenger chokeslammed the referee through the announce table before his own ally attacked a second official, ending the match without a decision; the two combatants were then shown to have secretly allied all along.

matches.stipulation: Tag Team Championship match
matches.note: The challengers won with a Backdrop Driver in the match's closing seconds after a grueling back-and-forth.

matches.stipulation: Canadian Heritage Championship match
matches.note: The challenger's own valet distracted the referee while a second valet passed him a bottle of liquor, which he poured into the champion's eyes before finishing him with a superkick.

matches.stipulation: Texas death match for the Great Lakes Championship
matches.note: A rival promotion's own president interfered at ringside, distracting the champion long enough for his challenger to hit an inverted DDT and win the title when the champion could not answer a ten count.

matches.stipulation: First-ever match for the newly created CCWA World Heavyweight Championship
matches.note: Both men lay motionless after a top-rope Death Valley Driver before the winner managed to drape an arm across his opponent for the count.

appearances.source: Interfered at ringside against the defending Great Lakes Champion, a rival promotion's own wrestler.

evidence.source: The promotion's own broadcast, now served in full.
evidence.note: Closes the three-day pay-per-view with four title changes and the first-ever defense of a newly created interfederation championship.

notes: The IIWA/MLW Extreme Championship match at the top of the card involves a title shared with a fourth, unrelated federation outside this record's own three-promotion alliance, and is not itself registered as a title in this record.

date.source: The card's own six-part newsgroup posting, 5 September 2001; the broadcast names no calendar date of its own.

matches.title: mlw-1999-maple-leaf
matches.stipulation: Opening match, made the first MLW Maple Leaf Championship match by Matt Muentes
matches.finish: Ogama spat red mist into Ormande's eyes behind the referee's back and pinned him with the Ogmacity to become the first Maple Leaf Champion.

matches.title: mlw-1999-heritage
matches.stipulation: MLW Canadian Heritage Title Match, one fall, 30-minute time limit
matches.finish: Rush hit a top-rope DDT and rolled it into a submission lock; the referee stopped it when Scythe's arm dropped three times.

matches.title: mlw-1999-true-north-tag-team
matches.stipulation: MLW True North Tag Team Title Match
matches.finish: Champions retained by disqualification: Viper Stinger-kicked his own partner and Team Hollywood swarmed Steppenwulf.

matches.stipulation: WarGames: The Match Beyond
matches.finish: Richman German-suplexed Dave Diamond off the top of the cage and Lord James Gray followed with a shooting star press for the pin.

matches.stipulation: The Ultimate Confrontation: Doc Toxic vs. Doc Toxic, no countout, no disqualification
matches.finish: With both referees gone, the promotion's president counted the pin himself for the masked impostor, who unmasked afterward as Major Victory.

matches.title: mlw-1999-heavyweight
matches.stipulation: Triple Threat Match for the MLW Heavyweight Title, Valtharius the Mad named special guest referee
matches.finish: De Sade pinned Helter Skinner while Bobby Toast, turning on the champion, held Sampson in the Wake-Up Call sleeper over the top rope.
